short: A series of political changes in Athens that stripped the aristocratic Areopagus council of its powers, ushering in the era of radical democracy.
full:
Taking advantage of the absence of his conservative rival Cimon, the statesman Ephialtes passed a series of laws targeting the Council of the Areopagus. This ancient council, composed of former archons serving for life, had long served as a bastion of aristocratic influence and a check on popular rule.

Ephialtes' reforms redistributed the traditional political and judicial powers of the Areopagus—leaving it jurisdiction only over homicide and some religious matters. The transferred powers were given to the Council of 500, the Assembly, and the popular law courts (heliaia). Ephialtes was assassinated shortly afterward, but his changes firmly established the radical democratic system later championed by his deputy, Pericles.
